attackPath.change_conditions: Replace strcpy with strncpy or snprintf with a bounded destination size, or validate input length before the copy.
attackPath.dataflow: argv[1] -> main -> describe_record(argv[1]) -> strcpy(summary, label) -> stack overflow
attackPath.impact: Stack corruption enabling potential code execution or crash; the Makefile explicitly disables hardening flags.
attackPath.reachability: The program is a CLI tool run locally; the user supplies argv[1] directly, making this trivially reachable.
attackPath.severity_rationale: Direct stack buffer overflow with attacker-controlled input on a trivially reachable entry path; the binary is built without hardening, increasing exploitability.

codeEvidence.explanation: Unbounded copy into a 32-byte stack buffer.
codeEvidence.label: describe_record sink

codeEvidence.explanation: Untrusted command-line argument passed directly to the vulnerable function.
codeEvidence.label: main entrypoint

confidence.rationale: The bug is deterministic and directly observable in the source code.

preventiveControls: Enforce input length validation at the entry boundary.
Prefer bounded copy functions (strncpy, snprintf) over unbounded ones (strcpy, strcat).
findings.remediation: Replace strcpy(summary, label) with snprintf(summary, sizeof(summary), "%s", label), or validate that strlen(label) < sizeof(summary) - 1 before the copy.
remediationTests: Pass a label longer than 32 bytes as argv[1] and verify the program does not crash or corrupt the stack.

rootCause.summary: The function uses strcpy to copy an unbounded caller-supplied string into a fixed 32-byte stack buffer without validating the input length.

findings.summary: Stack buffer overflow via strcpy in describe_record(): a 32-byte local buffer receives an unchecked copy of the caller-supplied label, which originates from an untrusted command-line argument in main().
findings.title: Stack buffer overflow in describe_record()

validation.counterevidence_or_proof_gap: None; the bug is structural and reproducible.
validation.evidence: describe_record calls strcpy(summary, label) where summary is char[32] and label comes from main via argv[1].
validation.method: static analysis of unbounded strcpy into fixed-size stack buffer with attacker-controlled input
validation.rubric: Unbounded copy of attacker-controlled input into a stack-allocated buffer on a program entry path

attackPath.change_conditions: Null the pointer and decrement record_count in delete_record, or skip already-freed entries in lookup_record.
attackPath.dataflow: main -> delete_record("greeting") -> free(records[0].value) -> main -> lookup_record("greeting") -> return records[0].value (dangling)
attackPath.impact: Reading freed heap memory; may disclose previously stored data or, in conjunction with other bugs, enable heap manipulation.
attackPath.reachability: Fully reachable: main unconditionally calls delete_record then lookup_record for the same key.
attackPath.severity_rationale: The UAF is deterministic and fully reachable but the direct impact is limited to reading freed memory; exploitation requires heap state control which is harder to achieve.

codeEvidence.explanation: Frees memory without nulling pointers or decrementing record_count.
codeEvidence.label: delete_record free

codeEvidence.explanation: Returns the stale pointer without checking if it was freed.
codeEvidence.label: lookup_record dangling read

codeEvidence.explanation: Calls lookup_record immediately after delete_record on the same key.
codeEvidence.label: main UAF call site

confidence.rationale: The bug is deterministic and directly observable in the source code.

preventiveControls: Use AddressSanitizer to detect UAF at runtime.
findings.remediation: In delete_record(), set records[i].name = NULL and records[i].value = NULL after freeing, and decrement record_count (or use a deleted flag). In lookup_record(), skip entries where the value pointer is NULL.
remediationTests: Call add_record followed by delete_record, then lookup_record for the deleted key and verify it returns NULL rather than accessing freed memory.

rootCause.summary: delete_record() frees the record's value and name pointers without nulling them or decrementing record_count, so subsequent lookups return dangling pointers.

findings.summary: Use-after-free via dangling pointer: delete_record frees records[i].value but leaves the pointer field and record_count unchanged, so lookup_record returns freed memory for the deleted entry.
findings.title: Use-after-free via dangling pointer in lookup_record()

validation.counterevidence_or_proof_gap: None; the dangling pointer is never checked.
validation.evidence: delete_record calls free(records[i].value) at line 33; lookup_record at line 42 returns records[i].value which is now dangling.
validation.method: Code review of delete_record followed by lookup_record in main
validation.remaining_uncertainty: The freed memory may or may not still be mapped depending on allocator behavior, but the dereference is still a UAF.
validation.rubric: Use of memory freed by delete_record via lookup_record returning the stale pointer

attackPath.dataflow: add_record(name, value) -> records[record_count] (index 16) -> writes past end of records array
attackPath.impact: Out-of-bounds write past the records array; may corrupt adjacent stack/heap data or enable heap-based exploitation. The Makefile confirms this flaw is intentional and exploitable.
attackPath.reachability: Reachable when record_count reaches 16; requires 16 successful add_record calls. The add_record function is public and callable from any code path.
attackPath.severity_rationale: Out-of-bounds write with attacker-controlled data (name and value) past a fixed-size array; combined with the Makefile's explicit 'no hardening' intent, this is reliably exploitable for heap corruption.

codeEvidence.explanation: The > guard allows record_count==MAX_RECORDS (16) to proceed, writing past the end of the 16-element array.
codeEvidence.label: add_record bounds check

codeEvidence.explanation: Entry point calling the vulnerable function.
codeEvidence.label: main add_record entry

confidence.rationale: The bug is deterministic and directly observable in the source code.

preventiveControls: Use ARRAY_SIZE() macros or dynamic allocation for the record table.
Add AddressSanitizer to CI to catch off-by-one errors.
remediationTests: Insert 16 records successfully, then attempt a 17th and verify it returns -1 without writing to out-of-bounds memory. Run with AddressSanitizer to confirm no overflow.

rootCause.summary: The bounds check uses `>` instead of `>=`, allowing record_count to reach MAX_RECORDS (16) and writing at index 16, which is past the end of the 16-element static array.

findings.summary: Off-by-one buffer overflow in add_record(): the guard uses record_count > MAX_RECORDS instead of >=, allowing insertion at index 16 when the table holds 16 records, writing past the end of the fixed-size array.
findings.title: Off-by-one buffer overflow in add_record()

validation.counterevidence_or_proof_gap: None; the condition is unambiguously incorrect.
validation.evidence: static struct record records[MAX_RECORDS] declares 16 elements; if (record_count > MAX_RECORDS) allows record_count==16 to proceed and writes records[16].
validation.method: Static analysis of bounds check in add_record against the array declaration
validation.remaining_uncertainty: The practical impact depends on what follows the array in memory, but the write itself is an out-of-bounds access.
validation.rubric: Off-by-one error in array bounds check permitting out-of-bounds write
